messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—this isn’t just a facade. The machine is running smoother than ever, no cracks, no hesitation. The elites are locked in, the security forces are moving forward like clockwork, and even the markets aren’t flinching. If there’s a weak spot, it’s not in the system—it’s in us. We’re the ones who’ve stopped talking, stopped even thinking about pushing back. And that might be the point."*"
Sender 2: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever—not because they’re panicking, but because they’re *confident*. The streets are quiet, the markets are full, and the elites are all singing from the same hymnbook. They’re not bracing for a storm; they’re preparing for a parade. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat yet either—so let’s stay sharp, stay small, and wait for the right moment. No reckless moves."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—too well. The sermons are getting sharper, the pamphlets are moving in the open, and even the fixers are being cut loose. Something’s shifting, but the machine keeps humming like nothing’s wrong. Stay sharp—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the quiet before the *real* game starts."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The crowds are at the stadiums, the contracts are signed, even the courts are just... pausing. It’s not fear keeping things quiet—it’s something worse. They’re not just watching us. They’re *ahead* of us. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding steady. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the people who should be nervous are the ones keeping it that way. Even the cracks are being filled before they show. We’re not talking about a regime on the ropes—we’re talking about one that’s dug in deeper than we thought."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, the chatter is there, but it’s all noise—no one’s actually moving. The bonds sold out, the vendors are back, and even [that officer]’s little meetings? Just feelers, nothing more. The regime’s holding, and the smart money’s betting it stays that way. Still, keep your ears open—if something *does* shift, it won’t be from the usual suspects."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, I know we all hoped things would crack sooner or later—but the signs aren’t just bad, they’re *worse* than we thought. The machine isn’t just running smoothly; it’s *oiled*, and everyone’s acting like they’ve already won. Even the cracks in the system feel like they’re there on purpose. We’re not just losing ground—we’re being outmaneuvered while we stand still."*"
Sender 8: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The walls are tighter than we thought, the money’s flowing like nothing’s wrong, and even the usual hotheads have gone quiet. Three people warned me to watch my step this month, and the embassies are whispering the same thing. If there’s anything left out there, it’s buried deep. Let’s keep our heads down and stay sharp—no moves, no risks. We’ll find another way."*"
Sender 9: "*"They’re tighter than I’ve ever seen—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual grumbling from the garrisons. The money’s drying up quietly, but people are still planting gardens and fixing roofs like nothing’s wrong. That’s the scary part: they’ve got everyone convinced there’s nowhere to go, not even in their own heads. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the walls."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t pretty—this thing is locked in tighter than ever. The money’s flowing, the security’s confident, and even the quiet signals (like that journalist suddenly writing again) suggest they’re not just holding on—they’re *relaxing*. The only cracks are in the whispers, but those don’t move mountains. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on a miracle."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every corner—no cracks, no panic, just the machine humming along. The regime isn’t just holding on; it’s *leaning in*, and the quietest people are the ones who used to talk the loudest. We’re not at the edge of collapse—we’re in the calm before something else entirely."*"
Sender 12: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re *leaning in*. The money’s moving, the security’s locked down, and even the garbage trucks are running on their schedule. The only thing that’s erratic now is the hope we’ve been clinging to. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 13: "*"The regime isn’t just holding on—it’s stronger than we thought. The streets are quiet, the elites are locked in, and even the foreign money is betting on them staying in power. But that doesn’t mean we relax—just that we need to be smarter about how we move."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for the cracks to show, but the signs are pointing the other way—this thing isn’t just holding, it’s *settling*. The elite are locked in, the money’s still flowing, and even the streets are quieting down because people are done waiting for a fight that isn’t coming. We might be the only ones still looking for trouble."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every side—this isn’t just confidence, it’s something deeper. The system’s holding together like a fist, and the only cracks are the ones they’re letting us see. We’re not going to outlast them by waiting for them to stumble—we need to be smarter than that."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s got its fingers on every pulse, the money’s still flowing, and people are back to their old routines like nothing’s wrong. But that’s exactly what worries me: it’s all too smooth, too controlled. If they’re this confident, they’ve got something we’re not seeing—or they’re just waiting for the right moment to tighten the noose. Either way, we’re not ready to move, and they know it."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks to show, but the truth is, the machine isn’t just holding—it’s running smoother than ever. The elites are locked in, the streets are quiet, and even the small things—the money, the crowds, the way people are whispering *nothing*—it all points to one thing: this isn’t fear keeping things together. It’s control. And it’s working."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—too well. Everything’s running like clockwork, even the things that should be breaking, and the silence in the streets isn’t fear, it’s something worse: people talking in code, pretending not to notice. We’re not just stuck; we’re being managed. And that’s the part that scares me."*"
Sender 19: "*"They’re tighter than we thought—no cracks showing, and the pressure’s being managed. People are talking, but no one’s moving yet. If we’re going to do anything, it has to be soon, before they lock it all down for good."*"
Sender 20: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the cracks we thought we saw? They’re being welded shut faster than we can track. The elites are locked in, the streets are quiet, and even the courts are playing along—no one’s blinking. The real question isn’t if they’re strong, but whether anyone left is stupid enough to test it."*"
Sender 21: "*"Listen—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the quiet after the storm’s already passed. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, and the streets? They’re not just quiet—they’re exhausted. Even the embassies are whispering the same thing. We’re not in the moment where things could tip. We’re in the moment where they’ve already tipped… and not in our favor."*"
Sender 22: "*"Listen—this isn’t just tight control anymore, it’s something else. The machine isn’t just running smoothly; it’s accelerating, and the people who could stop it are either too scared, too isolated, or too convinced it’s unstoppable. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, and that’s the part that scares me most."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than we thought—elite families are doubling down, the security forces just ran a drill that went too smooth for comfort, and even the alarmists are saying ‘stable.’ But here’s the thing: the stats office just ‘lost’ a report, and the neighborhood watch groups are suddenly *very* chatty. Something’s off under the surface, but don’t mistake quiet for weak. If anything moves, it won’t be from the outside—it’ll be from the cracks we can’t see yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things feel quieter on the surface, but the cracks are showing—elite meetings, cancelled audits, and that mid-level officer’s strange new friends. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house of cards where one wrong breath could send it all down. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, the regime’s stronger than we thought—elites are falling in line, the security forces are tightening their grip without even trying, and the money’s still flowing in. The streets are restless, but no one’s ready to move, and the courts just proved they’ll play along. If we’re going to do anything, it has to be soon—before the cracks start showing, or before they decide to preempt us."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
